messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Flonase is a nasal spray containing fluticasone propionate. Fluticasone propionate is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the lining of the nose.
Flonase Nasal Spray is used to treat nasal congestion, sneezing, runny nose, and itchy or watery eyes caused by seasonal or year-round allergies.
Flonase Allergy Relief is for use in adults and children who are at least 4 years old and is available without a prescription. Children's Flonase Allergy Relief contains the same medicine and is also for ages 4 and older.
Flonase Sensimist contains fluticasone furoate rather than fluticasone propionate and is approved for use in adults and children 2 years of age and older. Children's Flonase Sensimist is also for ages 2 and older. In Flonase Sensimist labeling, relief of itchy, watery eyes applies to ages 12 and older.
The brand-name prescription version of Flonase nasal spray has been discontinued in the United States. Generic fluticasone propionate nasal spray is still available by prescription, and over-the-counter Flonase products and store brands remain on the market.
Triples: [["Flonase Nasal Spray", "has generic name", "fluticasone propionate"], ["fluticasone propionate", "is a", "corticosteroid"], ["fluticasone propionate", "reduces", "inflammation in the lining of the nose"], ["Flonase Nasal Spray", "treats", "nasal congestion"], ["Flonase Nasal Spray", "treats", "sneezing"], ["Flonase Nasal Spray", "treats", "runny nose"], ["Flonase Nasal Spray", "treats", "itchy or watery eyes"], ["Flonase Allergy Relief", "has recommended age group", "adults and children who are at least 4 years old"], ["Flonase Allergy Relief", "is available without", "prescription"], ["Children's Flonase Allergy Relief", "contains same medicine as", "Flonase Allergy Relief"], ["Children's Flonase Allergy Relief", "has recommended age group", "ages 4 and older"], ["Flonase Sensimist", "contains", "fluticasone furoate"], ["Flonase Sensimist", "has recommended age group", "adults and children 2 years of age and older"], ["Children's Flonase Sensimist", "has recommended age group", "ages 2 and older"], ["Flonase Sensimist", "has age specific effect", "relief of itchy, watery eyes applies to ages 12 and older"], ["Flonase Nasal Spray", "has brand name status", "discontinued in the United States"], ["generic fluticasone propionate nasal spray", "is available by", "prescription"], ["over-the-counter Flonase products", "remain on", "market"], ["store brands of Flonase", "remain on", "market"]]
Relations: ["contains", "contains same medicine as", "has age specific effect", "has brand name status", "has generic name", "has recommended age group", "is a", "is available by", "is available without", "reduces", "remain on", "treats"]
Answer:

completion:
contains: The subject product includes or incorporates the substance or component specified by the object entity.  
contains same medicine as: The subject product contains the same active pharmaceutical ingredient as the product specified by the object entity.  
has age specific effect: The subject product has an effect or indication that applies only to the age group specified by the object entity.  
has brand name status: The subject product has a commercial or marketing status described by the object entity.  
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.  
has recommended age group: The subject product is recommended for use in the age group specified by the object entity.  
is a: The subject entity is classified as or belongs to the category specified by the object entity.  
is available by: The subject product is available through the method or requirement specified by the object entity.  
is available without: The subject product is available without the requirement specified by the object entity.  
reduces: The subject substance decreases or lessens the condition or effect specified by the object entity.  
remain on: The subject products continue to be available or present in the context specified by the object entity.  
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
